messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A job laid out across an entire bench. a small screw head strips at the last moment. You are tired of repeating the same approach. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i rub my palm and keep the screw head aside. i bend the bench edge down, then scrape a small notch in the head and test the screw head. if it slips, i stop and use the old approach. i do not repeat the head, just leave the bench empty and wait for the screw to move."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "I rub the screw head with my thumb. “same. same motion.” I move the bench closer. the screw stays in my hand. “keep one bolt.” then I pocket the loose bolt and leave the screw dangling."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "i rub the screw head back with my thumbnail, then put the bench back on. the screw stays on the edge, so i move it to the side. i put the chair back on, but the screw stays. i put the chair back on again, then put the bench back."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "I press the head with a knuckle, then run one short, flick-through motion across the bench. I leave the screw untouched for now, mark its scratch, and mark the stripped head with grease. I keep the bench’s original screw beside it."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "\"One stitch. Likely.\" You glance at the watch. \"The bench is moving. I keep it.\" You move the screw head closer, but stop when the watch ticks."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "you put the screw head down. you look at the bench. “not the same.” you move the head once. you keep the bench empty. you wait for the screw to strike the wood."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i touch the head. i look at the screw. i put the pen under the head. i move the board. the bench stays. i put the screw head beside the board. the same."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i stop moving and wipe the screw head once with my thumbnail. the bench shifts slightly, so i keep the screw. the job stays on the floor. i sit beside it and wait for the next pause. the screw makes a small indent, then stops. i leave it there and wait for the floor to move."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "I stop the seed tin beside the bench. The head moves. I stop beside the tin. I put the screw head beside it. \"You stand still.\" I look at the bench. \"The head moves too. I put my claw on the board.\" I leave the tin beside the dead nail. \"The bench stays.\""}, {"id": "R010", "response": "i press the screw head against the bench’s edge, then slide it under the scraper. i keep the screw head in place until the scraper clicks. then i turn the bench over and check the scraper."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "I rub my palm, turn the screw head a fraction, and scrape the bright edge with my thumbnail. \"I tried that last,\" I say. I scrape again, then turn the bench once. I scrape again, then leave the screw head alone."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "i tap the head, pause, and check the screw slot. i leave the bench alone, then check the last strip. i say sorry to the bench, then leave the job alone."}]
